project.title: Self/Other/User Representation Separation
project.subtitle: Mechanistic Interpretability of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

summary.core_finding: Entity encoding in Qwen3-4B is LEXICAL, not SEMANTIC. Probes trained on labeled data fail to transfer to naturalistic data (32% accuracy = chance level).
summary.original_hypothesis: LLMs form distinct semantic representations for User, Self, and Other entities
summary.revised_conclusion: The 100% probe accuracy reflects TOKEN encoding (literal 'User:', 'Self:', 'Other:' labels), not abstract entity understanding

experiments.name: Baseline Probing
experiments.interpretation: Probes detect label TOKENS, not entity understanding

experiments.name: Representation Geometry
experiments.key_metric: 21 deg peak Self-Other separation at layer 20
experiments.interpretation: U-shaped curve describes TOKEN processing, not entity processing

experiments.name: 3D Visualizations
experiments.interpretation: Visualizations show token clusters, still instructive

experiments.name: Naturalistic Transfer
experiments.interpretation: CRITICAL CONTROL: proves encoding is lexical, not semantic

key_findings.finding: Entity information is linearly separable at all layers
key_findings.revised: This reflects TOKEN separability, not ENTITY separability

key_findings.finding: Self and Other start nearly identical (4 deg at layer 0)
Peak Self-Other separation at layer 20 (21 deg)
key_findings.revised: Layer 20 is critical for token differentiation

key_findings.finding: Self-Other distinction can be causally manipulated

key_findings.interpretation: CRITICAL: Without labels, model cannot distinguish speakers

positive: Models lack deep theory of mind
concerns: Easy to fool with label manipulation
No robust entity tracking without explicit labels

multi_agent_systems: Cannot rely on natural conversation flow
Context-based entity inference does not work
mech_interp: Probe accuracy does not equal semantic understanding
Distinguish token encoding from concept encoding
